text: How do you expect to have faith in yourself if you can't even keep your own word?
context: From the 3 February 2025 letter, after he argues that compromising yourself for other people's favour is a score your subconscious keeps.

text: We sacrifice the thing we want (self worth) for the thing which is supposed to get it (validation).
context: The same letter: the approval we chase is only a roundabout way of trying to validate ourselves.

text: You must not outsource your sense of self-worth or you will live at the mercy of everyone's opinion.
context: From the 30 May 2023 letter on why caring what people think cannot be switched off, only turned down.

text: Other people's heads are a wretched place for your self-worth to live.
context: His closing line in that letter, after quoting Gurwinder Bhogal on the persona that captures an audience.

text: Failure can make you miserable but I'm not sure success will make you happy.
context: From the 28 March 2022 letter on the tension between wanting success and wanting to feel like enough.

text: External success won't fill an internal void.
context: He grants that some external success matters for status and respect, then draws this limit.

text: If your drive to succeed comes from a fear of insufficiency, and you continue to disprove those fears with success in the real world, and yet the feeling of insufficiency persists, what makes you think that the answer to this problem is more success?
context: His name for the loop: Insufficiency Adaptation. More proof does not retire the fear that asked for it.

text: The smartest people I know are hyper-aware of the limits of their knowledge.
context: The life hack in the 27 February 2023 letter: say you don't know, keep the ego small, and let someone improve your view.

text: Your weirdness is your competitive advantage. No one can beat you at being you.
context: From the 18 March 2024 list of realisations he says he has come upon.

text: You don't need motivation to do the thing. You just need to do the thing.
context: From the 3 June 2024 letter: preparation in imagination is not the same as the move itself.

text: Perfectionism is procrastination masquerading as quality control.
context: The same letter, on waiting to feel ready before leaving a job, starting a project, or asking someone out.

text: The results you get in life are going to come anyway. Your fears and neuroses about them are doing little other than making your journey toward achieving them more miserable.
context: From the 7 February 2022 letter. He prices the worry at about five percent of the outcome and calls the rest a tax on the trip.
